analysis.investment_thesis: Cigniti is a high-quality IT testing business (ROE 26%, ROCE 34%, near-zero debt) but at INR 3,571 Cr market cap it sits far outside my sweet spot, and its December 2024 absorption into Coforge as a subsidiary kills any independent multibagger story. The transformation narrative now belongs to Coforge, not Cigniti.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital efficiency: ROE 26%, ROCE 34.1%, D/E just 0.02 — virtually a debt-free business
Expanding profitability: operating margins 17%, FCF positive all 5 years, cash pile grew from 24 to 199 Cr (2022→2025)
Reasonable valuation: P/E 11.7x, EV/EBITDA 9x for a quality IT services business
key_risks: Subsidiary trap: Coforge acquired Cigniti in Dec 2024 — independent decision-making and growth story now subsumed into a large parent
Market cap 3,571 Cr is 3-4x above my preferred entry zone; meaningful re-rating is structurally limited from here
Revenue CAGR of 14.5% over 9 years is pedestrian for IT — global IT testing market is competitive, not niche or underpenetrated
red_flags: Coforge subsidiary: promoter is now a listed large-cap, not a hungry founder-entrepreneur with skin in the game
FII 11.6% + DII 9.3% = already institutionally discovered, no information asymmetry advantage
2017 net loss of -395 Cr (impairment/goodwill) reveals historical M&A risk — now repeating the M&A cycle via Coforge deal
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cigniti fails the SMILE test on the two most critical dimensions. At INR 3,571 Cr market cap it is more than 3x my upper comfort zone of ~1,000 Cr, meaning the re-rating potential from small-cap discovery is gone. More importantly, Cigniti is no longer an independent company — Coforge acquired it in December 2024, turning it into a subsidiary. The independent promoter story, the founder-led ambition, the ability to pivot quickly — all of this is now filtered through a large-cap parent's capital allocation decisions. My SMILE framework demands "large in aspiration" from a founder who is personally hungry; a subsidiary has its ambitions decided in a boardroom elsewhere.

The business fundamentals are genuinely impressive: ROCE of 34%, D/E of 0.02, FCF of 147 Cr in FY25 on a 2,014 Cr revenue base, and expanding margins. At P/E 11.7x this is not expensive in absolute terms. But I am not a value investor buying cheap businesses — I am a multibagger hunter looking for 10-50x. Cigniti's 9-year revenue CAGR of 14.5% and net profit CAGR of 16.7% are decent but not the 25-30%+ I need to justify the illiquidity risk of a single-stock concentrated bet. With institutions already present (FII + DII combined ~21%), the stock is discovered, and the upside from here is more of a steady compounder story — one better captured by owning Coforge directly.
